text.p: Italian bond futures drifted down in late afternoon trade undermined by the weakness in German bunds while U.S. economic data had little overall impact on the market, dealers said.
They added there was good domestic cash buying interest, but in the absence of any market-moving domestic news today futures drifted lower along with other European bond markets.
"We were all waiting for the U.S. figures, but in the end they gave little overall lead to European markets," said one trader on the LIFFE market.

U.S. September producer price rose 0.2 percent after a forecast of 0.3 percent giving U.S. Treasuries some comfort over inflationary fears, but retail sales showed a 0.7 percent rise in the same month compared to an expected 0.2 percent increase.
"The retail figures caused a bit of a surprise but this was dampened by a revised figure for August to a 0.2 percent fall from a 0.2 percent rise," said the trader.

Dealers said the mood on the Italian market remained generally positive with the lira steady throughout the day, but many investors were concerned by the heady Italian market when other European markets were falling.

Earlier, the market showed little reaction to comments late Thursday by Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio when he said Italian CPI was improving but September was not a good figure, and added that the 1997 budget might not be enough to meet the criteria set for the European single currency.
